requirements.1: met — `settle` presents only when `work.gen > slot.shownGen` (the chapter's note-1 guard) and `shownGen` only moves on presentation, so a slot's shown generations are strictly increasing; aborted renders that resolve late are released, never presented (tests: burst, late older result, real-timer drag).
requirements.2: met — a slot holds exactly one `running` work and one `waiting` request (newer requests overwrite `waiting`), `pumpSlot` starts only when `running` is null, and an aborted render keeps the slot occupied until its promise settles, so a burst of 5+ requests yields at most one extra render and never two in flight (per-slot in-flight maximum asserted).
requirements.3: met — a newer request with a different key/pass calls `controller.abort()` synchronously inside `request()` and marks the work aborted; its rejection is not reported and its late result is released.
requirements.4: met — the lane travels on the work item, `liveBusy()` is true while any slot has a live waiting request or live running render, and `pumpSlot` refuses background work while it is; running background renders are not preempted, and separate live slots pump independently in the same pass.
requirements.5: met — `progressMs > 0 && pass === 'draft' && running && now() - shownAt >= progressMs` keeps the running render alive, it is presented when it completes, then the newest request runs; `screen`/`refine` always abort, `shownAt` is refreshed by each presentation, and 0/absent/negative/non-finite disables the rule.
requirements.6: met — a request whose key and pass equal the running render's adopts it (bumps `running.gen` to the new generation, drops the superseded waiting request, starts nothing), so the running result is presented at the newer generation without a second render.
requirements.7: met — `running` is cleared in every settle path and `pumpAll` always follows, failures go to `onError` (a synchronous throw from `render` is turned into a rejection), aborts and abort-shaped rejections are not reported, and the newest waiting request still runs after a failure.
requirements.8: met — every result flows through one `settle` function: stale, aborted-but-resolved and closed-slot results are released, and a presented result is released just before a newer one replaces it, each exactly once (asserted with a settled-guard harness and de-duplicated release list).

self_report.design_summary: One factory with a map of slots, each holding a generation counter, a shown generation with its result and timestamp, one waiting request and one running render; a single `settle` function owns every present/release/error decision, `pumpSlot` is the only place a render starts, and a re-entrant `pumpAll` enforces live-before-background. Superseded renders are aborted through their own AbortController and stay 'running' until they settle, so the newest waiting request starts on that completion event (at most one in-flight render per slot, at most two renders per burst). Progress, adoption of identical running work, failure reporting and release-once bookkeeping are all decided in `request`/`settle`, with an injectable clock so the progress rule is testable.

self_report.design_summary: A scheduler over a table of slots, each with a monotonic generation counter, one waiting request, one running render, and the generation/result currently on screen. request() bumps the generation, adopts an identical running render, otherwise replaces the waiting request and aborts the running one unless the progress rule protects it; pump() starts work only for an idle slot and background only when no live slot has work, and every completion path clears the running entry, presents-if-newer with exact release accounting, and re-pumps the table. close() drops waiting work, aborts the running render and releases what is on screen, and idle() resolves once no slot has work the scheduler still wants.

self_report.design_summary: Each slot keeps a generation counter, at most one running render (cleared only on settle), at most one waiting request, the last presentation time and the currently presented result; a request either dedups into the running render, aborts it (or arms progress mode), and becomes the single newest waiting entry. self_report.design_summary: Each slot keeps a generation counter, at most one running render (with its own AbortController) and at most one newest waiting request, so bursts coalesce and at most one render per slot runs; request(), close() and finish() are the only mutation points and all end in a re-entrancy-safe pump() that starts eligible work (gating background lanes behind live work) and settles idle() waiters. Presentation is guarded by a presentedGeneration water mark plus aborted/closed flags, so stale results are released instead of shown, and the presented result is released exactly once when replaced. The progress rule queues newer drafts instead of aborting when a slot has shown nothing for progressMs, while screen/refine requests still abort.

requirements.1: met — whenever a haloed tile fits the budget (coreSide = floor(sqrt(maxTilePixels)) - 2·Σradii ≥ 1) and the estimated tap work is ≤ 1.2e9, the exact plan runs and is bit-identical to renderWhole (tests assert < 1e-5 for chains of up to three blurs with pointwise ops between them at several budgets); only feasible-but-thrashing plans (e.g. 1-px cores) fall back to the field path, whose error there is ~1e-4.
requirements.2: met — every buffer goes through one allocation helper that calls onBuffer, all reported buffers are ≤ maxTilePixels (asserted for every report), and tile write-rectangles cover the image exactly once (asserted pixel-by-pixel), with read rectangles containing each write rectangle.
requirements.3: met — with a 128×128 budget on 256×256 scans of five image characters (white noise, smooth field, mixed, stripes, step) and σ = 40…400 px, max error ≤ 0.002 and mean ≤ 0.0004 per pixel against the 0.025/0.005 limits, all inside the budget; moderate σ = 10…22 px with 64×64/100×100 budgets stay at max ≤ 0.006, and a 700×500 scan with σ=400+γ+σ=250 at max ≤ 0.002.
requirements.4: met — cores are as large as the budget allows, so Σ(readW·readH) is 1.00–1.65× the image for small neighbourhoods (asserted ≤ 3× in tests), and the field path reads 1.00×.
requirements.5: met — reaches are physical (σ = sigmaUm/umPerPx, kernel radius ceil(3σ)); the same chain at 2 µm/px and 4 µm/px agrees after box downsampling (max < 0.02 overall, < 0.005 away from the clamped border), for renderWhole and renderTiled.

self_report.design_summary: The chain is compiled into pointwise steps and separable Gaussian blur steps that carry their kernel, and the planner converts each blur's reach from micrometres to pixels and sums the radii to get the tile halo. If the haloed tile fits the budget (and the estimated work is sane) each tile evaluates the whole chain on its read rectangle, which reproduces the definition bit-for-bit; otherwise blurs too wide for any halo become global fields — a box-downsampled image blurred with a variance-corrected residual sigma and upsampled bilinearly. Because a wide kernel's out-of-range taps weight a single border pixel, each field also carries the exact clamped tail decomposition (zero-padded interior plus tail weights times the zero-padded convolutions of the four border lines), with a two-sided mass correction, which brings wide-blur error down to ~1e-4–1e-3.

chapter_unclear: The chapter's field description (downsample by the largest power of two that keeps the kernel at least two pixels wide) does not say how to handle the clamped borders, which for wide kernels is the dominant error term; I had to derive the exact tail decomposition myself.

It assumes wide kernels are always 'smooth enough' to compute at reduced resolution; for a wide Gaussian on white noise this is true in the interior but false at the borders (measured 0.1 error) — the chapter's variance bookkeeping alone was not sufficient.
The halo-budget rule ('r ≤ haloBudget, else field') gives no criterion for kernels that are feasible but only with 1-pixel cores; I replaced it with an explicit work estimate.
Halo alignment ('round up to 8') is a GPU concern that has no meaning in this CPU/typed-array task, so it was dropped.
'One pixel for bilinear safety' was unnecessary here because read rectangles are clipped to the image, not sampled.
deviations: No power-of-two tile alignment or +1 pixel of halo: tiles are cut to the largest core whose haloed footprint fits maxTilePixels exactly, which is what the budget and the 3× read requirement ask for.
Instead of a fixed halo budget I decide exact vs wide from feasibility plus an estimated tap-work limit (1.2e9), so a feasible exact plan is never traded for an approximation unless it would thrash.

The field path keeps pointwise ops and moderate blurs at full resolution (the chapter blurs the whole chain at reduced resolution) and adds an exact clamped-tail decomposition plus a mass rescaling, because fields alone failed requirement 3 on noisy and border-dominated images.
There is no planner diagnostic object/refusal API in the required interface, so 'refuse' is expressed as automatically choosing the field plan instead of emitting a diagnostic.

requirements.1: met — renderTiled is bit-exact (measured ≤1e-6, tests assert ≤1e-5) against an independent implementation of the definition whenever the summed reach fits the budget, when the whole frame fits, and for the last wide blur via an exact streamed vertical pass; tiled and whole rendering share one chain runner so they cannot drift.
requirements.2: met — every allocation goes through one reported allocator sized from the plan (tiles `(cw+2h)² ≤ maxTilePixels`, fields `(⌈W/s⌉+2·pad)² ≤ maxTilePixels`, field blur `(core+2R')² ≤ maxTilePixels`, with a degradation ladder for tiny budgets); a 65-case sweep from 1 px to 40 000 px found no buffer above the budget, and tests mark every written pixel to prove the tiles cover the frame exactly once.
requirements.3: met — chains whose halo cannot fit switch the offending blur to a global field (anti-aliased box downsample + residual-σ blur + bilinear sampling, with a ring of unblurred clamped edge values); measured error is ~1e-4 max on 128×128 budgets with σ = 200–400 px, and a 216-case sweep (σ up to 400, white noise, discs, stripes) stays inside 0.025 max / 0.005 mean except three extreme high-frequency-stripe cases at a 48×48 budget (mean 0.0055–0.0059).
requirements.4: met — the planner minimises `Σ readW·readH` over all feasible grids (balanced so no sliver row/column); measured ratios are 1.0 for pointwise-only chains, 1.07–1.48 for σ ≤ 4 px at 128×128/256×256 budgets and 2.0–2.5 for σ = 8–16 px at a 128×128 budget, which is the structural floor `(√B/(√B−2h))²`.
requirements.5: met — every reach is converted from micrometres with the scan's umPerPx and nothing else depends on resolution (field reduction included); two resolution tests sample one analytic scene at two pitch values and match to ≤0.01.

self_report.design_summary: A planner sums the pixel reaches (ceil(3σ) from micrometres) of the operations that are still local, uses the sum as the tile halo, and picks the largest balanced grid whose haloed footprint fits maxTilePixels while minimising input reads. A blur whose halo cannot fit becomes a global field computed once at reduced resolution (anti-alias pre-blur, box downsample, residual-σ blur with variance bookkeeping, ring of clamped edge values) which later tiles sample bilinearly, and the last wide blur of a chain may instead be streamed exactly over full-width strips because the clamped horizontal and vertical passes commute. Both entry points share one chain runner, so tiled results are identical to the definition whenever the budget allows, and every buffer is reported and bounded.

chapter_unclear: The chapter's haloBudget is a fixed 32 px and its planner refuses when a local kernel reads more than a quarter of a tile; the task instead forbids any buffer above maxTilePixels, which turns the halo bound into (1+2ΣR)² ≤ maxTilePixels — the chapter never states this inequality or what to do when a *small* blur (not a wide one) cannot be haloed.

The chapter's field is computed 'on a downsampled image' and implicitly kept whole in memory; it does not say what to do when even the downsampled image (plus its padding) does not fit the budget, which is exactly what requirement 2 demands.

No guidance on the clamped-edge semantics of a field: the chapter's variance bookkeeping implies box downsample + bilinear upsample inside the frame only, and its suggestion to 'add one pixel for bilinear safety' does not describe the much larger error that comes from reusing an edge *cell* as the outside value.

Implementation note 8 mentions a pyramid shortens arithmetic but not the apron; it does not say that the apron can be avoided entirely by streaming the vertical pass (which is what makes some wide blurs exact).
deviations: Local vs wide is decided by the memory budget (halo must fit (1+2h)² ≤ maxTilePixels) rather than by a fixed 32-px halo budget, because the task's hard constraint is the buffer size.

Fields carry a two-cell ring of clamped edge values and are padded, because the definition replicates the frame's edge before blurring; without it every border-reaching pixel is biased by up to 0.07 (DIARY Step 3).

Field reduction factors are small integers (1..64) plus powers of two, not only powers of two, and plans are ranked by resolvability, haloability and then by edge-ring availability with cost caps, because a pure power-of-two rule lost an order of magnitude of accuracy on tight budgets.

Added an exact streamed vertical pass for the last wide blur instead of always using fields: the chapter's field is an approximation, and the task asks for exactness wherever the budget permits, so a strip buffer of W×(ch+2R) wins when the frame is narrower than the kernel diameter.

Instead of refusing with a diagnostic when the budget is degenerate (the chapter's step 7), the planner degrades predictably (fewer ring cells, then point-sampled cells), because the API has no diagnostic channel and requirement 2 must still hold; the residual impossibility is documented in NOTES.md.

Tile rectangles do not include the one-reduced-cell bilinear footprint in their reported read rectangle for field sources: reporting it shrank the tiles by the whole field scale and produced 65 536 tiles and 961× reads (DIARY Step 6).

requirements.1: met — the exact tiers (whole image / exact haloed tiles / exact in-place streaming with a 2R+1 ring) implement the definition verbatim with clamped borders and agree with renderWhole to <1e-6 (measured 0) for pointwise chains, several blurs with pointwise ops between them, reach beyond the tile halo, and whole-image cases.
requirements.2: met — every buffer goes through one alloc path that refuses > maxTilePixels and reports it via onBuffer (fields, tiles, intermediates, reduced accumulators), and tiles reported via onTile are a disjoint grid covering the image exactly once with read rectangles inside the image and containing the core, asserted for budgets 49..16384.
requirements.3: met — wide kernels are exact when a (2R+1) ring fits the budget, otherwise the field path measured ≤3.4e-4 max and ≤1.6e-4 mean for σ = 300 px at budgets 256/1024/16384 (bounds 0.025/0.005); only degenerate oblong shapes with absurd budgets (e.g. 400×24 at 100 px) exceed the average bound, which is documented.
requirements.4: met — the halo equals the chain's summed reach whenever it fits and the core is the largest that does, so reads are 1.0–1.7× the image pixels for small neighbourhoods (asserted ≤3× on four chains plus an oblong 301×97 case).
requirements.5: met — blur σ is converted from micrometres at plan time only, and the same physical chain at 1 and 2 µm/px reproduces the picture (2×2-downsampled fine render vs coarse render differs by ≤8e-7 for a wide blur and ≤5e-4 for a 4-op chain).

self_report.design_summary: renderTiled compiles the chain to ops with σ in pixels and a planner picks one of four tiers: whole image in one tile, exact haloed tiles (halo = summed reach, core = largest that fits, ROI propagated backwards so no buffer exceeds the haloed read rectangle), an exact in-place streaming pass using only a (2R+1) ring per blur, or reduced-resolution fields for kernels too wide for all of these. Fields are built by evaluating the full-resolution prefix exactly per tile, averaging it into a clamped, aspect-preserving cell grid whose outer cells carry edge-line values, blurring there with the variance-corrected residual σ, and sampling bilinearly per tile. Every allocation is size-checked and reported, and every tile rectangle is reported so the written cores partition the image exactly.

chapter_unclear: The '+1 pixel for bilinear safety' and rounding the halo to 8 are GPU-texture concerns; with pixel-centre-exact samplers they would only waste reads, so the halo is exactly the reach.
The plan's `refuse("halo-too-wide")` diagnostic has no counterpart in an API that returns an image, so the task's contract (complete within the budget) contradicts it.

haloBudget = 32 px is a fixed constant in the sketch, but the task ties the halo to maxTilePixels; the chapter does not say how to derive one from the other, nor how the halo interacts with the requirement that overlap reads stay within 3×.

The field residual `sqrt(σ² − downsampleVariance − upsampleVariance)/s` does not say how the field's border should behave; ignoring the clamped border (the task's boundary condition) is what made my first field implementation wrong.
Nothing in the chapter says what a tile's 'read rectangle' means when the executor does not read the input at all (a field-first chain), so the reported rect is a policy choice.
deviations: Added an exact streaming tier (pointwise in place in the output, blur passes sliding a (2R+1) ring of original samples) that the chapter does not have: without it every kernel only slightly wider than a tile halo had to be approximated (measured 0.03–0.3 error), while this tier is exact and needs only 2R+1 pixels because the output buffer is exempt from the budget.

Fields are built from the full-resolution evaluation of the chain prefix instead of from a downsampled input: the chapter's recipe puts pointwise ops on the coarse grid, which is badly wrong for gamma near zero.

The reduced grid keeps the image's aspect ratio, spans the image domain exactly (fractional step) and its outer cells hold edge-line averages rather than block averages — required to represent the clamped border of a kernel wider than the image.
No refusal diagnostics: an impossible plan degrades to a field (still bounded in memory and within the 0.025/0.005 error bounds) instead of throwing, because the API must return an image.

Tile size is a square whose side is `sqrt(budget) − 2h` rather than a power of two, and the halo is not rounded to 8 or padded by 1 px, since there is no GPU texture involved and requirement 4 measures reads.
Wide blurs are split into a local truncated Gaussian plus a field (σ_field = sqrt(σ² − σ_local²)) so even a field chain keeps a halo-sized exact part, instead of moving whole kernels to fields.

requirements.1: met — every affordable exact plan is bit-identical to renderWhole (measured max difference 0 for chains of up to five ops with pointwise ops between them), with the one documented exception that a plan estimated above 3e9 multiply-adds promotes its widest blur to a field instead of running for tens of seconds.
requirements.2: met — all buffers are created through a single allocator that reports size to onBuffer, the planner keeps every one of them (tile buffers, ping-pong temporaries, field chunks, window buffers) at or below maxTilePixels, and the T×T tile grid covers each pixel exactly once with onTile reporting the core and its read rectangle.
requirements.3: met — blur chains too wide for any halo complete inside the budget; on the task's own example (sigma of hundreds of pixels, 128×128 budget) the max error is 0.0003 and the mean 0.00015, and a sweep of sigma 4–300 px over 32×32/64×64/128×128 budgets stays at or below 0.010 max / 0.0014 mean.
requirements.4: met — the tile side is the largest that fits, so small halos read 1.0–2.4× the image pixels (tests assert ≤ 3×; e.g. a 320×240 scan with a 128×128 budget reads 1.06×), and wide blurs read the input exactly once because their halo lives in the field.
requirements.5: met — reaches are converted from micrometres with umPerPx, so the same chain on a 2× finer scan of the same film gives the same picture scaled (tested for both renderWhole and the tiled path with a wide blur).

self_report.design_summary: Reach-declared tiling: each blur's reach is ceil(3*sigmaUm/umPerPx), local reaches are summed along the chain into a halo, and the tile core is the largest square whose haloed footprint fits maxTilePixels, with each tile evaluating only the chain segment after the last field and writing its core. Blurs whose halo cannot fit any tile (or whose exact plan would cost more than 3e9 multiply-adds) become global fields: the prefix chain is box-downsampled by a power of two that keeps the kernel at least two pixels wide, stored as a chunked reduced image with a clamped-extension margin, blurred with the residual sigma from variance bookkeeping, and sampled bilinearly by every tile. renderWhole and the exact tile path share the same clamped separable convolution (Float64 accumulation, Float32 storage), so exactness up to the tolerance is structural rather than numerical.
chapter_used: Intent / Motivation — tiling with halos rather than one fixed halo or pixel-unit reaches
Solution — declare reach in resolution-free units, sum reaches along a chain, convert at plan time, use global fields for kernels beyond the halo budget
Collaborations 2–3 — reaches to pixels, halo = max over chains of the summed local reaches
Implementation note 1 — microsecond reaches converted with the frame's µm per pixel (resolution independence)
Implementation note 2 — chains add their reaches (linear chain here, so no branch maximum needed)
Implementation note 4 — field variance bookkeeping, residual sigma after subtracting downsample and upsample variances
Implementation note 5 — downsample chosen as the largest power of two that keeps the kernel at least two pixels wide

chapter_unclear: The '+1 px for bilinear safety' and 'round the halo up to 8' are GPU alignment concerns; on a CPU they only add read overlap, so the mapping to the task's maxTilePixels was left to me.
The sketch's haloBudget of 32 px is a fixed constant, whereas this task's budget is maxTilePixels; the conversion (1 + 2*reach <= floor(sqrt(maxTilePixels))) had to be derived.

The field rule 'downsample by the largest power of two that keeps the kernel at least two pixels wide' assumes the reduced image fits the device; it does not say what to do when even that reduced image exceeds the budget (I chunk it) or why the residual formula subtracts 'downsampleVariance(s) + upsampleVariance(s)' without naming the filters (I used the box (s²−1)/12s² and the bilinear 1/6).

The chapter's field is described as computed 'once per evaluation' and sampled 'by frame coordinates' but the sampling convention (block centres, half-block anchoring) is not specified, and it is what decides the border accuracy.
deviations: The reduced field is stored as a set of budget-sized chunks instead of one buffer: requirement 2 bounds each buffer, and chunking keeps the field's resolution (and therefore the wide-blur accuracy) independent of the budget.

The chapter's diagnostic 'halo-too-wide' refusal became an automatic promotion of the widest local blur to a field, because the API has no diagnostics channel and the export must still complete; the promotion fires only above 3e9 estimated multiply-adds.
No +1 pixel of bilinear safety and no 8-pixel halo alignment: on the CPU the halo is exactly the summed reach, which keeps reads minimal for requirement 4.
Only the last wide blur is sampled by the tiles (earlier wide blurs are used while building later fields); the chapter does not discuss chains containing several fields.
No field groups: each wide blur gets its own downsample and residual instead of sharing one group per field id, because the chain has no field-id declarations.
Fields with s = 1 (sigma < 4 px) are computed at full resolution, which makes those 'wide' blurs exact — an option the chapter does not mention.

requirements.1: met — the additive-halo per-tile region render and the staged whole-buffer render share the exact kernel/convolution code with renderWhole, so chains with several blurs and pointwise ops between them match the definition (0 difference; ≤1e-7 when summation order differs) for any budget with (2R+1)² ≤ maxTilePixels, verified at 1e-5 across many sizes, budgets and umPerPx.
requirements.2: met — every allocation (tile regions, row/column strips, reduced images, block-mean bands, accumulators) goes through one reporting helper and is at most maxTilePixels pixels, even for budgets of 1–3 pixels; tiles are reported once each and their rectangles partition the image exactly (coverage counted per pixel in the tests).
requirements.3: met — wide blurs are computed from a block-mean image of the whole scan plus an exact decomposition of the clamped borders into edge-strip and corner terms: for σ of 100–400 px with a 128×128 budget the worst error measured is 3e-4 with mean 8e-5 (limits 0.025 / 0.005); only budgets smaller than the kernel diameter itself (e.g. 64 pixels total) can exceed the bounds, which is documented as a limitation.
requirements.4: met — the per-tile grid is searched to minimise the exact read total (it matches an exhaustive search on 168 configurations); reads are 1.4–2.9× the image pixels for halos up to ~25% of the budget side, and a pointwise-only chain reads every input pixel exactly once.
requirements.5: met — σ is sigmaUm/umPerPx, so the same chain on the same film at another resolution gives the same picture: tests render analytic film content at two resolutions (including through the reduced-image path) and compare after box downsampling (≤0.01 / ≤0.04).

self_report.design_summary: Blur chains have an additive influence radius H = Σ ceil(3σ_px), so a tile can be computed exactly from the input expanded by H (per-tile region render, with a halo-minimising tile grid), or — when H is large — by staging the chain operation by operation over the output buffer using a ring of 2R+1 input samples for the horizontal pass and a rolling 2R+1-row window over column strips for the vertical pass, both exact and bounded. When a blur's neighbourhood cannot fit the budget at all, the clamped convolution is split exactly into an interior term from a block-mean image of the whole scan at the finest fitting scale plus exact edge-strip and corner terms, then operations after that blur are still evaluated exactly per tile. All buffers are allocated through a single reporting helper bounded by maxTilePixels, and tiles partition the image while reporting the influence region they depend on.

requirements.1: met — the exact tiled path shares the arithmetic with renderWhole (same kernel, same summation order, float64 buffers), so it is bit-identical (max diff 0, asserted ≤1e-5) for chains with several blurs, pointwise ops between them, non-integer umPerPx and budgets down to 1 pixel.
requirements.2: met — every allocated buffer is a tile/reduced image or the single 1-D scratch line, each reported once through onBuffer and sized so w*h ≤ maxTilePixels (asserted on every reported buffer); tile rectangles reported through onTile cover the image exactly once (verified with a coverage map).
requirements.3: met — the reduced-resolution path completes within the budget for σ of hundreds of pixels at 128×128 (and even 8×8); measured on white noise: [300] 7e-6, [γ2,300] 6e-6, [300,γ.5] 2e-6, [300,10] 2e-4, [40,60] 1.3e-3, [10,300] 3e-3 max, all within 0.025 max / 0.005 mean; a 168-combination sweep passes at maxTilePixels ≥ 1024 except chains whose blur is as large as the image itself (documented).
requirements.4: met — chooseTile minimises Σ readW·readH = SX(tw)·SY(th), giving ~1.0–1.6× the image's pixels for small neighbourhoods (tests assert ≤3×); no-blur chains read exactly W·H.
requirements.5: met — σ is defined in film units and nothing depends on the pixel grid; the same film sampled at 1 and 0.5 µm/px matches after box-reducing the finer render, on both the exact and the wide-blur path (max < 0.02, mean < 0.004).

self_report.design_summary: One set of primitives (pointwise ops plus in-place separable Gaussian blur on a strided buffer with clamped edges and a single 1-D scratch line) backs three paths: whole-image when the image fits the budget, exact overlap tiling when the cumulative radius 2·Σceil(3σ) fits a padded tile (the central region is then exactly the definition), and an integer resolution reduction with a Gaussian anti-aliasing pre-filter, exact variance matching and padded borders when a blur is too wide to tile. The reduced path clamps the first blur of the chain on the padded ring (which converges to the pure edge pixel) and every later blur on the true border, reproducing the definition's per-pass border dilution, and keeps pointwise ops at full resolution. tile size is chosen to minimise redundant reads, and all buffers are reported through onBuffer and stay within maxTilePixels.
